issues.description: findChangedFiles return contract is silently widened from 'string[] | null' to optional, masking git failures
issues.detail: onTestRunStart coerces a null/undefined result from VitestGit.findChangedFiles into 'this.changedFiles = undefined', which is the same state as 'feature disabled.' The invariant the rest of the code relies on is 'changedFiles set => filter to these files; unset => include everything.' A git failure therefore reports coverage for ALL files — the opposite of what the user asked for. State the invariant explicitly and fail loudly (or set changedFiles to []) when git lookup fails.

issues.description: isIncluded membership test is O(n) per file via Array.includes inside a hot loop
issues.detail: Inside isIncluded, 'this.changedFiles.includes(filename)' is linear in the number of changed files and is called once per source file, giving O(F * C) overall where F = files audited, C = changed files. For large monorepos this is the wrong data structure. Promote changedFiles to a Set<string> at assignment time; lookup becomes O(1) and the cache layer still works.

issues.description: Path-shape invariant between changedFiles and the slashed/cleanUrl filename is never stated or proved
issues.detail: isIncluded now compares slash(cleanUrl(_filename)) against entries returned by VitestGit.findChangedFiles. The correctness of the equality test depends on git returning forward-slashed, absolute, query-stripped paths identical in shape to the audited filename — an unstated invariant. On Windows or with workspace roots this likely diverges silently and reports zero coverage. Normalize both sides through the same slash+resolve pipeline and document the postcondition.

issues.description: globCache is cleared after changedFiles is set, but cache keys do not encode the changedFiles identity
issues.detail: onTestRunStart calls globCache.clear() to invalidate prior decisions, which works for a single run but the cache key (filename) doesn't reflect that 'included' is now a function of (filename, changedFiles). If onTestRunStart is ever called twice in a process (watch mode, reruns) without a clear, stale answers leak. Either re-clear on every assignment or include a generation counter in the key.

issues.description: CLI transform for coverage.changed accepts strings but never validates them as plausible git refs
issues.detail: The transform normalizes 'true'/'false'/'yes'/'no' and otherwise passes the string through. A typo like '--coverage.changed HAED' silently becomes the literal ref 'HAED'; VitestGit will fail downstream and (per Issue 1) coverage will then quietly include everything. A literate-programming comment stating 'any non-boolean string is forwarded to git as a ref; validation happens in VitestGit' would at least make the contract explicit.

issues.description: Inheritance rule 'coverage.changed undefined => coverage.changed = changed' lacks a stated invariant for the false case
issues.detail: resolveConfig only inherits when coverage.changed === undefined. The test confirms 'changed=false' overrides inheritance, which is the intended behavior, but the code has no comment explaining the three-valued logic (undefined = inherit; false = explicit opt-out; truthy = explicit ref). Future maintainers reading this will not know whether 'undefined' is reachable from user config or only from defaults. Add a one-line invariant comment.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The feature is well-motivated and the tests exercise the happy paths nicely, but several invariants the implementation relies on are unstated, and one data-structure choice (Array.includes against changedFiles in the per-file hot path) is wrong for any non-trivial repository. The most worrying issue is silent semantic collapse: a null return from VitestGit.findChangedFiles is indistinguishable from 'feature disabled,' so a transient git failure flips the behavior from 'only changed files' to 'all files' with no warning. Path-shape equality between git output and the cleanUrl+slash filename is also load-bearing and unproved; on Windows or with non-root cwds this is the kind of bug that would only surface in user reports. Recommend: hoist changedFiles to a Set, fail loudly on git lookup failure, and add a literate comment block above isIncluded stating the (filename, changedFiles) invariant and the path-normalization contract.
